1.1.text:
Article 10

The family in efforts to protect the rights of women is obliged to:

a. protect women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades the dignity of women; b. provide equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and
c. prevent violations of women's rights within the household.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Dharmasraya Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration of Dharmasraya Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Dharmasraya.
4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Dharmasraya Regency.
5. Social Service, Women's Empowerment Child Protection Population Control and Family Planning hereinafter referred to as the Service is the Regional Apparatus that handles affairs in the Field of Women and Child Protection Implementation.
6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from abandonment, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or postremedial protection (assistance and treatment).
7. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy carried out rationally and systematically to achieve and realize gender equality and justice in a number of aspects of human life, through policies and programs that take into account the experiences, aspirations, needs and problems of women and men into the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of all policies and programs in various fields of life and development.
8. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja Gender Mainstreaming is a consultation forum for implementers and mobilizers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region.
9. Gender Mainstreaming Focal Point is an apparatus in the Regional Apparatus who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.

10.Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including children still in the womb.

11. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

12. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children.

13.Child Forum is a forum for child participation established with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is implemented with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking.

14.Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.

15.Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.

16.Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.

17.Trafficking in persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that person, whether done within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.

18.Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community.

19.Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions properly.

20.Law enforcement is the action of an apparatus authorized by the state to implement legislation.

21.Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.

22.Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving region to the region of origin.

23.Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

24.Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence.

25.Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the soul through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26.Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.

27.Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 28.Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a direct line up or down to the third degree.

29.Customs are eternal and hereditary conduct from one generation to another as an inheritance, so strong is its integration with the behavior patterns of society.

CHAPTER IV

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDRENPart One

Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women and Children

Article 30

(1) Reports of acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of victims, families of victims, the community and/or community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.

(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:

a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
(3) Further provisions regarding the procedures for handling complaint services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 72

(1) The Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

(2) The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises: a. the formulation of policies and regulations used as guidelines and standards in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection; b. technical guidance and training, comprising:

1. providing training for government officials and law enforcers on the prevention and handling of violence;
2. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
3. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
4. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and
5. providing training to Gender Mainstreaming working groups and focal points of each Regional Apparatus for preparing program activities based on gender-responsive planning and budgeting.
c. provision of facilities and infrastructure in organizing women's empowerment and child protection.
d. facilitation of the establishment of nagari that care for women and children; e. provision of information through print and electronic media related to the protection of women and children. (3) The supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises: a. monitoring carried out in the form of submission of reports on the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs by the Head of the Regional Apparatus to the Regent periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months; and b. evaluation of the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months conducted by the relevant Regional Apparatus
(4) The results of supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) constitute evaluation material for the women's empowerment and child protection program policy.
(5) Further provisions regarding Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent's Regulation.

Article 7

The obligations of the Regional Government in efforts to protect women include:

a. establishing and implementing policies, programs and activities for the protection of women's rights; b. cooperating with the community and/or Community Organizations in the implementation of women's protection in accordance with statutory regulations;
c. conducting rehabilitation and empowerment of women who are victims of violence; d. providing special protection to women victims of violence and human trafficking; and e. taking preventive measures in order to prevent violations of women's rights.

Article 36

(1) Assistance services as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (3) letter d are carried out for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.

(2) In providing assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1), P2TP2A may cooperate with persons or institutions that have expertise in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy.

Article 75

This Regional Regulation comes into force on the date of promulgation. In order that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placement in the Regional Gazette of Dharmasraya Regency. Enacted in Pulau Punjung on 27 December 2018

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them is dignity, worth, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the generation that will carry on the ideals of the nation, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate, and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, it is hoped that women will give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and of quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and the state, resilient generations will be born who will carry on the ideals of the nation. As Indonesian citizens, women also have the right to improve their quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and worth.

Women and children need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects for venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so on. As assets and hopes of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development.

To realize women's empowerment and child protection, support from legislation that can guarantee its implementation is needed.

Although the protection of women's and children's rights has been regulated in national-level legislation, the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children as well as the improvement of the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, so in providing protection to women and children, the Regional Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection regulates the scope as follows: a. women's and children's rights;

b. obligations;

c. improvement of women's quality of life;

d. protection of women and children;

e. improvement of family quality;

f. gender and child data system;

g. fulfillment of children's rights;

h. child-friendly regency; and

i. guidance and supervision.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 34

(1) Provision of safe houses as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (2) letter b may be provided by the Regional Government for women and children who experience criminal and/or civil problems.

(2) Safe house provision services as referred to in paragraph (1) aim to protect women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) Criteria for women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems who require safe houses include:

a. their lives are threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community; c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

Article 37

(1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (3) letter e constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement statutory regulations in order to handle criminal and/or civil problems against women and children, particularly to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

(3) Types of legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. legal assistance in the reporting process and preparation of official examination reports;
b. legal assistance in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office; c. legal assistance in the examination process at court; d. legal assistance in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision; and e. legal assistance in the mediation process. (4) The Regional Government provides legal assistance to women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems based on the provisions of statutory regulations.
(5) In providing legal assistance as referred to in paragraph (3), UPTD PPA may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other gender-sensitive legal companions.

Article 57

(1) Every Child has the right to obtain education and teaching in order to develop his/her personality and level of intelligence in accordance with interests and talents.

(2) Every Child has the right to receive Protection in educational units from sexual crimes and Violence committed by educators, education personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.

Part Four

Obligations of Family and/or Parents Paragraph 1 Obligations Regarding the Protection of Women

Article 9

(1) The obligations of the community in efforts to protect women and children:

a. to participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs against violations of the rights of women and children;
b. to provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
c. to monitor the law enforcement process in cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
(2) Ninik mamak, alim ulama and cadiak pandai as well as bundo kanduang are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and children.
(3) The obligations of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are based on statutory regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 64

The Regional Government is obligated to provide Social Welfare for:

a. children in conflict with the law; b. child victims of violence who are economically exploited; c. children who do not have parents and are cared for by parties or families who are unable;
d. child victims of natural disasters or social disasters; and e. children with disabilities.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them is dignity, worth, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the generation that will carry on the ideals of the nation, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate, and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, it is hoped that women will give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and of quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and the state, resilient generations will be born who will carry on the ideals of the nation. As Indonesian citizens, women also have the right to improve their quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and worth.

Women and children need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects for venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so on. As assets and hopes of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development.

To realize women's empowerment and child protection, support from legislation that can guarantee its implementation is needed.

Although the protection of women's and children's rights has been regulated in national-level legislation, the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children as well as the improvement of the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, so in providing protection to women and children, the Regional Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection regulates the scope as follows: a. women's and children's rights;

b. obligations;

c. improvement of women's quality of life;

d. protection of women and children;

e. improvement of family quality;

f. gender and child data system;

g. fulfillment of children's rights;

h. child-friendly regency; and

i. guidance and supervision.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them is dignity, worth, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the generation that will carry on the ideals of the nation, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate, and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, it is hoped that women will give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and of quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and the state, resilient generations will be born who will carry on the ideals of the nation. As Indonesian citizens, women also have the right to improve their quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and worth.

Women and children need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects for venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so on. As assets and hopes of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development.

To realize women's empowerment and child protection, support from legislation that can guarantee its implementation is needed.

Although the protection of women's and children's rights has been regulated in national-level legislation, the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children as well as the improvement of the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, so in providing protection to women and children, the Regional Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection regulates the scope as follows: a. women's and children's rights;

b. obligations;

c. improvement of women's quality of life;

d. protection of women and children;

e. improvement of family quality;

f. gender and child data system;

g. fulfillment of children's rights;

h. child-friendly regency; and

i. guidance and supervision.

b. obligations;

c. improvement of women's quality of life;

d. protection of women and children;

e. improvement of family quality;

f. gender and child data system;

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them is dignity, worth, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the generation that will carry on the ideals of the nation, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate, and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, it is hoped that women will give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and of quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and the state, resilient generations will be born who will carry on the ideals of the nation. As Indonesian citizens, women also have the right to improve their quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and worth.

Women and children need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects for venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so on. As assets and hopes of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development.

To realize women's empowerment and child protection, support from legislation that can guarantee its implementation is needed.

Although the protection of women's and children's rights has been regulated in national-level legislation, the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children as well as the improvement of the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, so in providing protection to women and children, the Regional Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection regulates the scope as follows: a. women's and children's rights;

b. obligations;

c. improvement of women's quality of life;

d. protection of women and children;

e. improvement of family quality;

f. gender and child data system;

g. fulfillment of children's rights;

h. child-friendly regency; and

i. guidance and supervision.

Article 72

(1) The Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

(2) The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises: a. the formulation of policies and regulations used as guidelines and standards in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection; b. technical guidance and training, comprising:

1. providing training for government officials and law enforcers on the prevention and handling of violence;
2. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
3. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
4. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and
5. providing training to Gender Mainstreaming working groups and focal points of each Regional Apparatus for preparing program activities based on gender-responsive planning and budgeting.
c. provision of facilities and infrastructure in organizing women's empowerment and child protection.
d. facilitation of the establishment of nagari that care for women and children; e. provision of information through print and electronic media related to the protection of women and children. (3) The supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises: a. monitoring carried out in the form of submission of reports on the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs by the Head of the Regional Apparatus to the Regent periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months; and b. evaluation of the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months conducted by the relevant Regional Apparatus
(4) The results of supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) constitute evaluation material for the women's empowerment and child protection program policy.
(5) Further provisions regarding Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent's Regulation.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them is dignity, worth, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the generation that will carry on the ideals of the nation, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate, and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, it is hoped that women will give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and of quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and the state, resilient generations will be born who will carry on the ideals of the nation. As Indonesian citizens, women also have the right to improve their quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and worth.

Women and children need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects for venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so on. As assets and hopes of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development.

To realize women's empowerment and child protection, support from legislation that can guarantee its implementation is needed.

Although the protection of women's and children's rights has been regulated in national-level legislation, the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children as well as the improvement of the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, so in providing protection to women and children, the Regional Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection regulates the scope as follows: a. women's and children's rights;

b. obligations;

c. improvement of women's quality of life;

d. protection of women and children;

e. improvement of family quality;

f. gender and child data system;

g. fulfillment of children's rights;

h. child-friendly regency; and

i. guidance and supervision.

Article 9

Article 37

(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

Article 34

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them is dignity, worth, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the generation that will carry on the ideals of the nation, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate, and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, it is hoped that women will give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and of quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and the state, resilient generations will be born who will carry on the ideals of the nation. As Indonesian citizens, women also have the right to improve their quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and worth.

Women and children need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects for venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so on. As assets and hopes of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development.

To realize women's empowerment and child protection, support from legislation that can guarantee its implementation is needed.

Although the protection of women's and children's rights has been regulated in national-level legislation, the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children as well as the improvement of the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, so in providing protection to women and children, the Regional Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection regulates the scope as follows: a. women's and children's rights;

b. obligations;

c. improvement of women's quality of life;

d. protection of women and children;

e. improvement of family quality;

f. gender and child data system;

g. fulfillment of children's rights;

h. child-friendly regency; and

i. guidance and supervision.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them is dignity, worth, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the generation that will carry on the ideals of the nation, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate, and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, it is hoped that women will give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and of quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and the state, resilient generations will be born who will carry on the ideals of the nation. As Indonesian citizens, women also have the right to improve their quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and worth.

Women and children need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects for venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so on. As assets and hopes of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development.

To realize women's empowerment and child protection, support from legislation that can guarantee its implementation is needed.

Although the protection of women's and children's rights has been regulated in national-level legislation, the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children as well as the improvement of the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, so in providing protection to women and children, the Regional Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection regulates the scope as follows: a. women's and children's rights;

b. obligations;

c. improvement of women's quality of life;

d. protection of women and children;

e. improvement of family quality;

f. gender and child data system;

g. fulfillment of children's rights;

h. child-friendly regency; and

i. guidance and supervision.

Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from abandonment, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or postremedial protection (assistance and treatment).

Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy carried out rationally and systematically to achieve and realize gender equality and justice in a number of aspects of human life, through policies and programs that take into account the experiences, aspirations, needs and problems of women and men into the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of all policies and programs in various fields of life and development.

(1) The Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

(1) Assistance services as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (3) letter d are carried out for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them is dignity, worth, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the generation that will carry on the ideals of the nation, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate, and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, it is hoped that women will give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and of quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and the state, resilient generations will be born who will carry on the ideals of the nation. As Indonesian citizens, women also have the right to improve their quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and worth.

Women and children need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects for venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so on. As assets and hopes of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development.

To realize women's empowerment and child protection, support from legislation that can guarantee its implementation is needed.

Although the protection of women's and children's rights has been regulated in national-level legislation, the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children as well as the improvement of the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, so in providing protection to women and children, the Regional Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection regulates the scope as follows: a. women's and children's rights;

b. obligations;

c. improvement of women's quality of life;

d. protection of women and children;

e. improvement of family quality;

f. gender and child data system;

g. fulfillment of children's rights;

h. child-friendly regency; and

i. guidance and supervision.

Article 7

The obligations of the Regional Government in efforts to protect women include:

a. establishing and implementing policies, programs and activities for the protection of women's rights; b. cooperating with the community and/or Community Organizations in the implementation of women's protection in accordance with statutory regulations;
c. conducting rehabilitation and empowerment of women who are victims of violence; d. providing special protection to women victims of violence and human trafficking; and e. taking preventive measures in order to prevent violations of women's rights.

Article 9

(1) The obligations of the community in efforts to protect women and children:

a. to participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs against violations of the rights of women and children;
b. to provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
c. to monitor the law enforcement process in cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
(2) Ninik mamak, alim ulama and cadiak pandai as well as bundo kanduang are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and children.
(3) The obligations of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are based on statutory regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 37

(1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (3) letter e constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement statutory regulations in order to handle criminal and/or civil problems against women and children, particularly to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

(3) Types of legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. legal assistance in the reporting process and preparation of official examination reports;
b. legal assistance in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office; c. legal assistance in the examination process at court; d. legal assistance in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision; and e. legal assistance in the mediation process. (4) The Regional Government provides legal assistance to women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems based on the provisions of statutory regulations.
(5) In providing legal assistance as referred to in paragraph (3), UPTD PPA may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other gender-sensitive legal companions.

Article 10

The family in efforts to protect the rights of women is obliged to:

a. protect women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades the dignity of women; b. provide equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and
c. prevent violations of women's rights within the household.

Article 64

The Regional Government is obligated to provide Social Welfare for:

a. children in conflict with the law; b. child victims of violence who are economically exploited; c. children who do not have parents and are cared for by parties or families who are unable;
d. child victims of natural disasters or social disasters; and e. children with disabilities.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them is dignity, worth, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the generation that will carry on the ideals of the nation, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate, and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, it is hoped that women will give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and of quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and the state, resilient generations will be born who will carry on the ideals of the nation. As Indonesian citizens, women also have the right to improve their quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and worth.

Women and children need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects for venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so on. As assets and hopes of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development.

To realize women's empowerment and child protection, support from legislation that can guarantee its implementation is needed.

Although the protection of women's and children's rights has been regulated in national-level legislation, the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children as well as the improvement of the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, so in providing protection to women and children, the Regional Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection regulates the scope as follows: a. women's and children's rights;

b. obligations;

c. improvement of women's quality of life;

d. protection of women and children;

e. improvement of family quality;

f. gender and child data system;

g. fulfillment of children's rights;

h. child-friendly regency; and

i. guidance and supervision.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Paragraph 1

Rights of Women

Article 56

(1) Every organizer of an educational unit must provide opportunities for Children to obtain educational services without discrimination.

(2) Every organizer of an educational unit is prohibited from expelling Children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the Child's education.

(3) In the event that a Child victim of an act of Violence experiences school dropout, then the child victim of violence shall be provided with formal and non-formal education, in this case carried out by the organizer of the educational unit and in coordination with the Women and Children Empowerment Unit

Article 34

(1) Provision of safe houses as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (2) letter b may be provided by the Regional Government for women and children who experience criminal and/or civil problems.

(2) Safe house provision services as referred to in paragraph (1) aim to protect women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) Criteria for women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems who require safe houses include:

a. their lives are threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community; c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

Article 73

Financing for the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection activities is sourced from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget and other legitimate and non-binding sources

Article 37

(1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (3) letter e constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement statutory regulations in order to handle criminal and/or civil problems against women and children, particularly to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

(3) Types of legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. legal assistance in the reporting process and preparation of official examination reports;
b. legal assistance in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office; c. legal assistance in the examination process at court; d. legal assistance in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision; and e. legal assistance in the mediation process. (4) The Regional Government provides legal assistance to women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems based on the provisions of statutory regulations.
(5) In providing legal assistance as referred to in paragraph (3), UPTD PPA may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other gender-sensitive legal companions.

Paragraph 4

Social Rehabilitation

4.1.text:
Article 72

(1) The Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

(2) The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises: a. the formulation of policies and regulations used as guidelines and standards in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection; b. technical guidance and training, comprising:

1. providing training for government officials and law enforcers on the prevention and handling of violence;
2. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
3. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
4. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and
5. providing training to Gender Mainstreaming working groups and focal points of each Regional Apparatus for preparing program activities based on gender-responsive planning and budgeting.
c. provision of facilities and infrastructure in organizing women's empowerment and child protection.
d. facilitation of the establishment of nagari that care for women and children; e. provision of information through print and electronic media related to the protection of women and children. (3) The supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises: a. monitoring carried out in the form of submission of reports on the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs by the Head of the Regional Apparatus to the Regent periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months; and b. evaluation of the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months conducted by the relevant Regional Apparatus
(4) The results of supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) constitute evaluation material for the women's empowerment and child protection program policy.
(5) Further provisions regarding Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent's Regulation.

Article 7

The obligations of the Regional Government in efforts to protect women include:

a. establishing and implementing policies, programs and activities for the protection of women's rights; b. cooperating with the community and/or Community Organizations in the implementation of women's protection in accordance with statutory regulations;
c. conducting rehabilitation and empowerment of women who are victims of violence; d. providing special protection to women victims of violence and human trafficking; and e. taking preventive measures in order to prevent violations of women's rights.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Dharmasraya Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration of Dharmasraya Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Dharmasraya.
4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Dharmasraya Regency.
5. Social Service, Women's Empowerment Child Protection Population Control and Family Planning hereinafter referred to as the Service is the Regional Apparatus that handles affairs in the Field of Women and Child Protection Implementation.
6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from abandonment, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or postremedial protection (assistance and treatment).
7. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy carried out rationally and systematically to achieve and realize gender equality and justice in a number of aspects of human life, through policies and programs that take into account the experiences, aspirations, needs and problems of women and men into the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of all policies and programs in various fields of life and development.
8. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja Gender Mainstreaming is a consultation forum for implementers and mobilizers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region.
9. Gender Mainstreaming Focal Point is an apparatus in the Regional Apparatus who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.

10.Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including children still in the womb.

11. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

12. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children.

13.Child Forum is a forum for child participation established with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is implemented with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking.

14.Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.

15.Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.

16.Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.

17.Trafficking in persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that person, whether done within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.

18.Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community.

19.Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions properly.

20.Law enforcement is the action of an apparatus authorized by the state to implement legislation.

21.Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.

22.Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving region to the region of origin.

23.Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

24.Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence.

25.Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the soul through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26.Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.

27.Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 28.Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a direct line up or down to the third degree.

29.Customs are eternal and hereditary conduct from one generation to another as an inheritance, so strong is its integration with the behavior patterns of society.

Article 10

The family in efforts to protect the rights of women is obliged to:

a. protect women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades the dignity of women; b. provide equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and
c. prevent violations of women's rights within the household.

Article 9

(1) The obligations of the community in efforts to protect women and children:

a. to participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs against violations of the rights of women and children;
b. to provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
c. to monitor the law enforcement process in cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
(2) Ninik mamak, alim ulama and cadiak pandai as well as bundo kanduang are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and children.
(3) The obligations of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are based on statutory regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDRENPart One

Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women and Children

Article 56

(1) Every organizer of an educational unit must provide opportunities for Children to obtain educational services without discrimination.

(2) Every organizer of an educational unit is prohibited from expelling Children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the Child's education.

(3) In the event that a Child victim of an act of Violence experiences school dropout, then the child victim of violence shall be provided with formal and non-formal education, in this case carried out by the organizer of the educational unit and in coordination with the Women and Children Empowerment Unit

Article 47

Communication, information and education as referred to in Article 46 letter a constitute communication activities to increase knowledge and improve the attitudes and behavior of families and communities in the Population and family planning Program.

Article 20

Efforts to enhance the role, quality and capacity of women in the field of law include: a. conducting socialization to increase women's legal knowledge and awareness; b. mapping and reviewing gender-biased policies; c. involving women's organizations in the process of drafting and discussing Regional legal products related to women's participation;

Article 30

(1) Reports of acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of victims, families of victims, the community and/or community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.

(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:

a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
(3) Further provisions regarding the procedures for handling complaint services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 57

(1) Every Child has the right to obtain education and teaching in order to develop his/her personality and level of intelligence in accordance with interests and talents.

(2) Every Child has the right to receive Protection in educational units from sexual crimes and Violence committed by educators, education personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.

Article 75

This Regional Regulation comes into force on the date of promulgation. In order that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placement in the Regional Gazette of Dharmasraya Regency. Enacted in Pulau Punjung on 27 December 2018

17.Trafficking in persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that person, whether done within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them is dignity, worth, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the generation that will carry on the ideals of the nation, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate, and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, it is hoped that women will give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and of quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and the state, resilient generations will be born who will carry on the ideals of the nation. As Indonesian citizens, women also have the right to improve their quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and worth.

Women and children need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects for venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so on. As assets and hopes of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development.

To realize women's empowerment and child protection, support from legislation that can guarantee its implementation is needed.

Although the protection of women's and children's rights has been regulated in national-level legislation, the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children as well as the improvement of the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, so in providing protection to women and children, the Regional Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection regulates the scope as follows: a. women's and children's rights;

b. obligations;

c. improvement of women's quality of life;

d. protection of women and children;

e. improvement of family quality;

f. gender and child data system;

g. fulfillment of children's rights;

h. child-friendly regency; and

i. guidance and supervision.

Article 11

(1) Parents in efforts to protect the rights of children are obliged to:

a. care for, maintain, educate, and protect children; b. develop children in accordance with their abilities, talents, and interests;
c. provide formal and non-formal education; d. guide children to behave in accordance with religion, ethics and morals as well as customs; and e. prevent marriage at child age. (2) In the event that parents are absent, or their whereabouts are unknown, or due to some reason, cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1) may be transferred to the family.

Article 37

(1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (3) letter e constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement statutory regulations in order to handle criminal and/or civil problems against women and children, particularly to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

(3) Types of legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. legal assistance in the reporting process and preparation of official examination reports;
b. legal assistance in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office; c. legal assistance in the examination process at court; d. legal assistance in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision; and e. legal assistance in the mediation process. (4) The Regional Government provides legal assistance to women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems based on the provisions of statutory regulations.
(5) In providing legal assistance as referred to in paragraph (3), UPTD PPA may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other gender-sensitive legal companions.

a. protect women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades the dignity of women; b. provide equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and
c. prevent violations of women's rights within the household.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them is dignity, worth, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the generation that will carry on the ideals of the nation, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate, and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, it is hoped that women will give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and of quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and the state, resilient generations will be born who will carry on the ideals of the nation. As Indonesian citizens, women also have the right to improve their quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and worth.

Women and children need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects for venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so on. As assets and hopes of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development.

To realize women's empowerment and child protection, support from legislation that can guarantee its implementation is needed.

Although the protection of women's and children's rights has been regulated in national-level legislation, the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children as well as the improvement of the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, so in providing protection to women and children, the Regional Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection regulates the scope as follows: a. women's and children's rights;

b. obligations;

c. improvement of women's quality of life;

d. protection of women and children;

e. improvement of family quality;

f. gender and child data system;

g. fulfillment of children's rights;

h. child-friendly regency; and

i. guidance and supervision.

Article 72

REGIONAL REGULATION OF DHARMASRAYA REGENCY

NUMBER 16 OF 2018

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them is dignity, worth, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the generation that will carry on the ideals of the nation, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate, and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, it is hoped that women will give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and of quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and the state, resilient generations will be born who will carry on the ideals of the nation. As Indonesian citizens, women also have the right to improve their quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and worth.

Women and children need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects for venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so on. As assets and hopes of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development.

To realize women's empowerment and child protection, support from legislation that can guarantee its implementation is needed.

Although the protection of women's and children's rights has been regulated in national-level legislation, the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children as well as the improvement of the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, so in providing protection to women and children, the Regional Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection regulates the scope as follows: a. women's and children's rights;

b. obligations;

c. improvement of women's quality of life;

d. protection of women and children;

e. improvement of family quality;

f. gender and child data system;

g. fulfillment of children's rights;

h. child-friendly regency; and

i. guidance and supervision.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Part Five

Enhancement of Role, Quality, and Capacity of Women in the Field of Law

Part One

Rights of Women and Children

Article 27

(1) The implementation of UPTD PPA services is integrative, carried out under one roof or networked to provide optimal services to women and children who experience problems.

(2) In the event that the implementation of UPTD PPA services as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out under one roof, UPTD PPA is responsible for carrying out the entire process in one unit to provide the necessary services to women and children who experience problems.

(3) In the event that the implementation of UPTD PPA services as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in a networked manner, UPTD PPA is responsible for the entire referral process for services needed by women and children who experience problems.

(4) Every element within the UPTD PPA environment in carrying out its duties must apply the principles of coordination, integration, synchronization, accountability and transparency, both within the UPTD PPA environment, as well as in relations between Regional Apparatuses, relevant agencies, and community elements.

The obligations of the Regional Government in efforts to protect women include:
